sections.heading: Two staggered windows — your two independent shots
sections.body: The EPOS deadlines are PER-COURSE, and your two viable economics courses have DIFFERENT windows. Göttingen: 1 Oct – 15 Nov 2026. Hohenheim: 15 Nov – 15 Dec 2026, with English accepted until 6 Jan 2027. EPOS allows up to 3 courses with ONE motivation letter, so you apply to both — two independent chances at the same €992/month, from one letter, a month apart.

sections.heading: You apply to the UNIVERSITY, not to DAAD

sections.heading: The four-step selection process
sections.body: 1. You send your complete application directly to the course. 2. A selection committee proposes candidates for a scholarship. 3. Suggested candidates are contacted by DAAD to upload to the DAAD Portal. 4. Final selection is made. Keep a copy of EVERY document — you re-upload all of them as PDFs if proposed.

sections.heading: What DAAD does NOT cover
sections.body: DAAD: 'DAAD does not pay tuition fees for its scholarship holders.' Baden-Württemberg charges non-EU master's students €1,500/semester. TUM charges €4,000–6,000/semester. Göttingen (Lower Saxony) charges none. Hohenheim waives it for EPOS recipients.

sections.heading: The motivation letter is a hard gate
sections.body: DAAD: 'you have to submit one motivation letter explaining why you are applying for these specific courses and why you chose that priority. If this information is ignored, the application cannot be considered or an already awarded scholarship might be withdrawn.'

sections.heading: DAAD's published selection criteria
sections.body: Professional qualification: academic achievements and GRADE DEVELOPMENT, language knowledge, relevant internships/work experience. Quality of the study project: preparation, choice of programme, host university, establishment of contacts. Potential of the applicant: motivation, prospects, extracurricular commitment and SOCIAL COMMITMENT. This is why your CFA, your treasury role, your teaching of colleagues and your first-generation background are not decoration — they map onto named criteria.

sections.heading: Advantages that are easy to miss
sections.body: No age limit — 'there is usually no fixed age limit.' No APS certificate needed for Bangladesh (APS is required only for India, China and Vietnam). Degree recency extensions are available for care responsibilities, illness, disability and military service — declare them in the 'Other comments' field and it can rescue eligibility.

sections.heading: Why this is your best fit
sections.body: It is the only scheme verified that funds tuition AND living costs, has Bangladesh on the country list, AND explicitly covers FINANCE programmes. It breaks the development-economics trade-off, because you can pursue Banking & Finance rather than development economics.

sections.heading: The two-stage trap
sections.body: SISGP states you must be 'admitted (or conditionally admitted) to one of the eligible master's programmes on the day of admissions announcements... Master's programmes to which you are listed as a reserve cannot be considered. There are no scholarships available for late admissions.' So the university application is not groundwork — it IS the gate.

sections.heading: Your work-experience maths
sections.body: Bangladesh applicants need ≥3,000 hours acquired prior to February 2026, from a MAXIMUM OF THREE EMPLOYERS. You have bKash (Oct 2023–Jan 2024 ≈ 680 hrs) plus City Bank (Mar 2024–Feb 2026 ≈ 4,160 hrs) = ~4,840 hours from 2 employers. You clear it comfortably and have one employer slot spare.

sections.heading: The leadership gate is real
sections.body: SISGP requires 'demonstrated leadership experience from a current or previous employer, or from civil society engagement.' Your evidence: teaching derivatives to treasury colleagues; representing City Bank at BAFEDA/BAMDA; the Level 2 award for the cross-divisional MIS dashboard; the Manager promotion; Joint Secretary of the BUP Economics Club; Cadet Corporal in BNCC and House Leader.

sections.heading: The timing
sections.body: Swedish university application: ~16 Oct 2026 – 15 Jan 2027 via universityadmissions.se, and you must PAY THE FEE. The SI portal is open for TWO WEEKS ONLY, ~9–25 Feb 2027, closing at 14:59 CET on the final day.

playbooks.title: Professor outreach — when it matters and when it doesn't

sections.heading: The fork in the road — decide this first
sections.body: For a THESIS-BASED master's, a specific professor must agree to supervise you — no supervisor means no admission in most Canadian research programmes, so outreach is decisive. For a COURSE-BASED master's (MFin, MFE, taught MA) a central admissions committee allocates funding by formula, and a professor replying 'good luck' changes nothing. Decide which you are pursuing before sending a single email.

sections.heading: Where it helps, and where it wastes time
sections.body: HELPS: research/thesis master's supervision; RA and TA positions funded from a professor's own grant; nomination-based scholarships; being named in a statement of purpose. WASTES TIME: taught master's admissions; DAAD EPOS (a course-level committee decides — contact the coordinator, not faculty); Erasmus Mundus (consortium staff run admissions); SISGP (a central body decides after you are admitted).

sections.heading: The correct contacts in Europe
sections.body: For Göttingen EPOS, contact the EPOS Study Coordinator (epos-devecon@uni-goettingen.de), not professors. For Hohenheim, contact agecon@uni-hohenheim.de. These are the people who know the answer. Professors at those departments do not run EPOS admissions.

sections.heading: Timing, to the hour
sections.body: Send Tue–Thu only (never Monday backlog, never Friday). Send so the email lands at the top of their inbox at the start of their working day. Their 8:30 am in Toronto is 6:30 pm in Dhaka; Calgary is 8:30 pm; Vancouver is 9:30 pm. Germany is 12:30 pm. Best months: September–mid-November, then January–February. Worst: mid-December–early January, and July–August.

sections.heading: The email itself
sections.body: Under 200 words. One specific paper named correctly, with year — this alone puts you in the top few percent. ONE clear, small, answerable question. Attach a one-page CV and nothing else. No flattery. Never mass-mail: academics talk to each other and it is a small field.

sections.heading: Ask structure, not charity
sections.body: Don't ask 'can you fund me?' Ask 'Are you accepting master's students for Sept 2027, and is funding in your department available to international students or mainly through research assistantships?' An easy question gets a reply. A vague request for help gets deleted.

sections.heading: Realistic expectations
sections.body: Cold emails from unknown international applicants get replies 10–25% of the time. A 20% reply rate on 30 emails means 6 conversations — that is a SUCCESSFUL campaign. Silence is the norm, not a verdict on you. Follow up once at 10–14 days, once more at 3–4 weeks, then stop.

sections.heading: Why tuition-free is not funded
sections.body: Germany's public universities charge little or no tuition, but that is not funding. You still must prove roughly €12,000/year in a blocked account (Sperrkonto) for the visa, plus €70–430 per semester in contributions. For a Bangladeshi applicant the blocked account is often the real wall, not tuition. So the honest goal is: tuition-free PLUS a monthly stipend.

sections.heading: A scholarship replaces the blocked account
sections.body: DAAD's own finance page states acceptable visa proof is 'an allocated amount on a blocked account' OR 'proof of receipt of a recognised scholarship.' So a full scholarship GENUINELY REPLACES the blocked account requirement.

sections.heading: But a scholarship does NOT bypass the visa queue
sections.body: The Dhaka embassy's appointment backlog is a separate administrative constraint. A fully funded candidate can still miss an intake because the appointment came too late. Verify current wait times with the German Embassy Dhaka and build that into your intake choice. UNVERIFIED: current Dhaka wait times.

sections.heading: The layers you can stack
sections.body: 1. Tuition: tuition-free public university, EPOS waiver at Hohenheim, or EMJM full tuition. 2. Living costs: EPOS €992/mo, EMJM €1,400/mo, SISGP SEK 12,000/mo. 3. Top-ups: DAAD rent subsidy to €350/mo, family allowance. 4. Earned income: TA/RA ships — but DAAD deducts income above €603/month gross from the stipend. 5. Blocked account: your own money, returned monthly. 6. Employer sponsorship: City Bank — completely untested, and worth asking, because you are being promoted and building the desk's analytics.

sections.heading: Germany — the strongest combined package
sections.body: 18-month post-study job-seeking visa. EU Blue Card with a 2026 graduate concession giving the LOWER salary threshold (€45,934.20) — this matters because a first job out of a master's will not pay €50,700. Blue Card → permanent residence in 21 MONTHS with German B1, versus ~33 months with only A1. B1 is therefore a FINANCIAL decision worth roughly a year of your life. The 2026 thresholds should be re-verified: sources differ slightly.

sections.heading: Switzerland — best money, worst residency
sections.body: 6-month job search after graduation (versus Germany's 18). Quota-limited work permits with a labour-market test. A 10-year C-permit where student years likely do NOT count. EPFL pays CHF 40,000 plus housing, but Switzerland is the inverse of Germany: excellent short-term money, poor long-term residency.

sections.heading: Canada — best residency, no funding
sections.body: Master's graduates are FULLY EXEMPT from the PGWP field-of-study restriction. A 3-year PGWP is available for master's graduates even for programmes under two years (≥8 months) since 15 February 2024. Master's students are exempt from PAL/TAL from 1 January 2026. But there is NO federal scholarship for an incoming international master's student — CGRS-M requires Canadian citizenship or PR. Canada converts a master's into PR more reliably than any European option, if you can solve the funding at programme level.

sections.heading: The language barrier in finance — the decisive unknown
sections.body: Finance and banking roles are far more local-language-dependent than tech. Germany's finance sector generally requires German. Sweden, the Netherlands, Switzerland and Ireland have relatively stronger English-language finance markets. This remains INCOMPLETE research — and it is decisive for your plan, because a funded development-economics degree in a country where you cannot work in finance serves neither goal.

sections.heading: The CFA in Europe
sections.body: Your charter is EQF/RQF Level 7 — master's level. It is your strongest differentiator and it compensates for the 3.30 CGPA by supplying exactly the quantitative proof the transcript lacks. It is also evidence of scarce skill, which is relevant to visa sponsorship. UNVERIFIED: how much weight European finance employers give it relative to a target-university master's.

playbooks.title: Erasmus Mundus — the verified economics shortlist

sections.heading: The value, now verified
sections.body: €1,400/month × up to 24 months = €33,600, plus the funded programme CANNOT charge scholarship holders tuition or mandatory participation costs, plus travel and installation. Total value roughly €51,600. Verified from multiple primary consortium sources, not an aggregator.

sections.heading: Your verified economics shortlist — exactly 3
sections.body: The Commission selected 37 new Joint Masters in July 2026 for September 2027 entry. Only THREE are economics: EGEI (Economics of Globalisation and European Integration, coordinator Italy/Bari — BEST FIT, ~15 scholarships/yr, partners in Lille, Ghent, Xiamen, Santander, Valparaíso, Tartu); GLOBAL COOP (Economic Policies for New Global Cooperation and Alliances, coordinator Brazil); GLODEP (Global Development Policy, coordinator Czechia — but this is DEVELOPMENT, the same trap as Göttingen). The cap is 3, so this is your clean shortlist.

sections.heading: 🔴 The 10% nationality cap — a real throttle
sections.body: EPOG-JM states it plainly: 'in order to ensure geographical diversity among students, no more than 10% of the students selected for a scholarship should have the same nationality.' If a consortium awards ~15 scholarships, only ~1–2 can go to any single nationality. Your odds therefore depend partly on how many other Bangladeshis apply that year — which you cannot control. This is precisely why EMJM alone cannot carry your portfolio.

sections.heading: The Partner Country advantage you already qualify for
sections.body: As a Bangladeshi citizen you are a PARTNER COUNTRY student — provided you have not lived, studied or worked in an EU Programme Country for more than 12 months in the last 5 years. You qualify. That unlocks the higher travel band: €3,000/year travel plus €1,000 installation for locations 4,000 km or more from the coordinator. Bangladesh qualifies.

sections.heading: ⚠️ The value discrepancy you must resolve
sections.body: EGEI's own page quotes €1,000/month. The current EMJM framework is €1,400/month. EGEI's page reflects the OLDER EMJMD action. EGEI also states scholarships are 'not offered in academic year 2026-2027' because the programme is relaunching under the new selection. Treat €1,400 as current, but VERIFY both points against EGEI's 2027/28 call before relying on them.

sections.heading: Where to apply, and when
sections.body: There is NO central EU application — you apply directly to each consortium. Consortia publish their 2027/28 calls from around mid-November 2026, with deadlines typically October to January. Watch epog.eu, master-egei.eu and the EACEA catalogue. The EACEA RSS feed (eacea.ec.europa.eu/node/253/rss_en) is the workaround that renders when the filtered catalogue will not.

sections.heading: The traps, named
sections.body: QEM (Models & Methods of Quantitative Economics) — the top search result for 'Erasmus Mundus economics' — awards NO EMJM scholarship; its consortium and excellence scholarships cover TUITION ONLY. EMLE awards real scholarships but needs 240 ECTS (unverified for your BSS), IELTS 7.0, and it is law-and-economics. EPOG-JM is a genuine economics EMJM but heterodox and ecological in focus, not finance.

sections.heading: 💡 A precedent worth exploiting for Eiffel
sections.body: EPOG-JM coordinates Eiffel applications on behalf of its second-year Paris students: 'The EPOG team will be in charge of coordinating the application with the eligible students.' That is a working example of a programme acting as your EIFFEL NOMINATOR — which is otherwise your hardest gate, since only French institutions may submit. Cite this precedent when you email French programmes.

playbooks.title: Canada — the 16-month gate that decides everything

sections.heading: 🔴 HIS WIFE IS COMING — CONFIRMED, NON-NEGOTIABLE
sections.body: Confirmed 7 October 2026. This makes the 16-month rule ABSOLUTE, not a preference. There is no fallback to a 12-month programme and no 'she arrives later' variant. A 12-month programme is functionally WORTHLESS no matter how good its placement or funding. This is now the single hardest filter in the entire pipeline — harder than funding, harder than grades.

sections.heading: 🚨 THE HARD GATE — verified verbatim from canada.ca
sections.body: Spousal open work permit: 'Starting January 21, 2025, your spouse or common-law partner may be eligible for an open work permit if you have a valid study permit and you're either studying in a MASTER'S DEGREE PROGRAM OF 16 MONTHS OR LONGER, studying in a doctoral degree program, participating in an eligible program, or studying in one of the following professional degree programs at a university: DDS/DMD, LLB/JD/BCL, MD, OD, PharmD, BScN/BSN/BNSc/BN, BEd, BEng/BE/BASc.' Effective 21 January 2025. Work permit duration: 'Most of the time, your spouse or common-law partner's work permit will be valid for the same period of time as your study permit.'

sections.heading: 💡 THE KEY STRATEGIC INSIGHT — search the WRONG departments and you find nothing
sections.body: Canadian ECONOMICS MA programmes are overwhelmingly 12 months and therefore automatically excluded. The programmes that genuinely run 16–24 months with a funded thesis live in MATHEMATICS, STATISTICS, ACTUARIAL SCIENCE, FINANCIAL MATHEMATICS and business-school research MSc routes. Quebec is structurally advantaged because its MSc programmes are often two years (four sessions) rather than 12 months.

sections.heading: ⭐ THE FINDING SO FAR: Waterloo MMath (thesis option)
sections.body: MMath in Statistics and MMath in Actuarial Science are RESEARCH-BASED and FUNDED. Waterloo's own funding page: 'Full-time MMath students (in good academic standing) in the Master's Research Paper stream are normally funded for one year (3 academic terms). Students that successfully switch to the Thesis stream will be provided one additional term of funding.' 3 terms (12 months) + 1 thesis term = 4 terms = 16 MONTHS — exactly the threshold. Funding = guaranteed TA in the offer letter + scholarships + supervisor GRA/GRS. Deadline: priority 15 Dec 2026, FINAL 6 Jan 2027, fall admission only.

sections.heading: ⚠️ THE CRITICAL CAVEAT you must not miss
sections.body: All students are ADMITTED to the Master's Research Paper stream. The thesis switch must be requested AFTER the first term and 'normally an average of 90% or higher is required', plus supervisor and department approval. So the 16-month length is NOT guaranteed at admission — it depends on earning a 90% average in term one. That is a real risk, not a formality. Admission minimum is a four-year bachelor's in a quantitative discipline with a 78% average (your 3.30/4.00 ≈ 82.5% clears it).

sections.heading: 🔴 THE TRAP: Waterloo MQF looks perfect and is unfunded
sections.body: The Master of Quantitative Finance is 16 months — it PASSES the length rule — and has the best career outcomes found anywhere in Canada: 100% internship placement in most years (16/16 in 2024, 15/15 in 2023, 18/18 in 2022), with employers including RBC, TD Securities, Scotiabank, CIBC, BMO, CPP Investments, OTPP, CDPQ, OMERS, OPTrust, Manulife, Deloitte, KPMG, Polar Asset Management and Optiver. Alumni have gone to Bank of Canada, Barclays, Bloomberg NY, Citigroup, Deutsche Bank, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley and UBS Hong Kong. BUT the department states plainly: 'Part-time students and students in coursework or professional programs, such as the MActSc and MQF, do not receive funding.' It is listed as 'Master's, Professional'. It fails the funding constraint.

sections.heading: ⚙️ MAILING IS PARALLEL-OPTIONAL
sections.body: You asked that outreach can be deferred if needed but must run in parallel and never block the applications that actually close. Operating rule: PRIORITY 1 are the hard deadlines (Göttingen EPOS 15 Nov, EPFL and Hohenheim 15 Dec, Swedish university application 15 Jan, SISGP 9–25 Feb). PRIORITY 2 are the unblockers (IELTS, City Bank letters, BUP ranking and ECTS, certified translations). PRIORITY 3 is Canada outreach, which is QUEUED, NOT URGENT — professor emails have no deadline and stay valuable for months. If a week is consumed by the EPOS pack, the emails simply slide to the next Tue–Thu window. Nothing is lost. But note Waterloo's MMath deadline is 6 January 2027, so Wave 1 should go by mid-November to leave room for a reply.

sections.heading: ✉️ CONTACT DETAILS — ⚠️ ONE UNRESOLVED CONFLICT
sections.body: ⚠️ TWO DIFFERENT SENDER ADDRESSES ARE IN PLAY AND YOU MUST SETTLE THIS BEFORE SENDING ANYTHING. You told me professors should see santohasib.bup@gmail.com. But the existing 11 drafted emails say to send from hasibulhassan650@gmail.com. These conflict. RECOMMENDATION: use santohasib.bup@gmail.com — you confirmed it, it is already the address on your CV, and one guide notes that a new address can land in spam while an established one does not. Whichever you pick, the address on the CV you attach MUST match the address you send from. LinkedIn is linkedin.com/in/hasibul-hasan-santo.

sections.heading: 🔴 THREE ERRORS FOUND IN THE EXISTING EMAIL DRAFTS
sections.body: 1) CALGARY IS CLOSED. The draft to Apostolos Serletis says you plan to apply to Calgary's thesis-based MA in Economics. Calgary's own Economics page states verbatim: 'The department of Economics is not accepting applications for the MA Thesis based program. Students are encouraged to apply for the MA Course based program.' My earlier exclusion of Calgary was CORRECT; the new file is wrong. BUT the funding claim is real — Calgary guarantees MA/MSc thesis students a minimum of $25,455/yr for internationals — so redirect the approach to a Calgary thesis programme that IS admitting (Mathematics & Statistics, or Haskayne). 2) KALIMIPALLI (Laurier) HAS NO VERIFIED PAPER — the source admits 'I could not verify a specific title', so that email has an empty paragraph 2, which is the one paragraph every guide says must name a real paper. DO NOT SEND IT. 3) SASKATCHEWAN EDWARDS 'funding guaranteed both years' is UNVERIFIED, and the file itself says funding comes automatically with admission — so the Tannous email buys supervisor fit, not money.

sections.heading: Funding mechanism — what changes in the email
sections.body: DEPARTMENT-FUNDED: funding comes WITH admission (TA/RA ship, entrance award). The professor does not control the money — ask about supervision and what to highlight for the department's funding decision. SUPERVISOR-FUNDED: funding depends on a professor's grant (NSERC, SSHRC, Mitacs, RA). The professor controls the money — ask DIRECTLY about a funded RA position. Waterloo's MMath is department-funded, so the Schied and Weng drafts ask about supervision and funding consideration, not for cash.

sections.heading: The verified professor lead
sections.body: Alexander Schied — Professor, Munich Re Chair in Stochastic Finance, University Research Chair, and MQF Program Director, Department of Statistics and Actuarial Science, Waterloo. Research includes risk measurement and management, robustness and model uncertainty, and MARKET MICROSTRUCTURE AND PRICE IMPACT — the closest match in Canada to a money-market desk role. Verified 2024 paper: Luo, Schied & Xue, 'The perturbation method applied to a robust optimization problem with constraint', Mathematics and Financial Economics vol. 18 no. 4. Profile: uwaterloo.ca/statistics-and-actuarial-science/profile/aschied — confirm the email address on that page; never guess an address format.

sections.heading: Send timing (Dhaka, UTC+6)
sections.body: Tuesday–Thursday, 8:00–10:00 recipient local time. Max 5 per day. NEVER two professors in the same department on the same day. DST changes 1 Nov 2026: Ontario/Quebec is 6:00–8:00 pm Dhaka before, 7:00–9:00 pm after. Avoid Mondays, Fridays, weekends, Thanksgiving 12 Oct 2026, Remembrance Day 11 Nov, reading weeks and December exam weeks. Follow up once at 10 business days, then stop.

subjectFit.subject: MSc Management (Finance)
subjectFit.whatItIs: At most Canadian business schools this is a generalist management degree with a finance concentration — organisational behaviour, marketing and strategy alongside finance electives. It is not a quantitative finance degree.
subjectFit.trap: The label says Finance; the content often does not. Genuinely quantitative exceptions: HEC Montréal's MSc streams and Laurier's research-based MSc Management (Finance).
subjectFit.admissions: GMAT/GRE usually required. Work experience valued. A 3.30 GPA is not disqualifying here.
subjectFit.funding: Almost never funded — these are revenue programmes. Saskatchewan Edwards claims funding guaranteed for both years, but the page 404s and I could not verify it.
subjectFit.lengthGate: Varies. Edwards is ~2 years. Verify per programme.
subjectFit.career: Corporate finance, banking relationship management, general management. Not quant, not trading, not risk modelling.
subjectFit.note: Viable only at Saskatchewan Edwards, and only if that funding claim is true.

subjectFit.subject: MSc Finance
subjectFit.whatItIs: A taught professional master's: corporate finance, investments, portfolio management, derivatives, some econometrics. Closer to the CFA curriculum than any other option.
subjectFit.admissions: GMAT/GRE almost always. Competitive on GPA.
subjectFit.funding: In Canada, MSc Finance at a business school is overwhelmingly UNFUNDED. These are the highest-margin degrees universities sell — a UBC Sauder or Rotman MSc Finance costs CAD $60k+ with no stipend.
subjectFit.lengthGate: Often 12–16 months, which may FAIL the 16-month spousal gate.
subjectFit.career: Corporate finance, investment banking, asset management. Good outcomes — but only if you can pay, and only if the length clears 16 months.
subjectFit.note: Concordia's 24-month MSc Finance is the notable exception and is already in the pipeline.

subjectFit.subject: MSc Financial Economics
subjectFit.whatItIs: The hybrid — economics core plus finance. Econometrics, asset pricing, monetary economics. Taught jointly by economics and business faculties.
subjectFit.admissions: Quantitative background expected. Less GMAT-dependent than MSc Finance.
subjectFit.funding: Mixed. Because it sits in economics faculties it is more likely to be funded than MSc Finance — but few Canadian universities offer this exact degree.
subjectFit.lengthGate: Varies. Did not confirm a Canadian version at 16+ months.
subjectFit.career: Central banking, research, risk, policy. Excellent fit for the sovereign-curve research interest.
subjectFit.note: Availability in Canada is limited. Worth checking HEC Montréal and Queen's.

subjectFit.subject: MA / MSc Economics
subjectFit.whatItIs: Core graduate economics: micro, macro, econometrics. The most academically rigorous and the most direct route to the research he wants.
subjectFit.admissions: Usually no GMAT. Quantitative and economics background expected.
subjectFit.funding: Economics MAs are the most likely to be funded — but the 12-month length makes that irrelevant for his gate.
subjectFit.lengthGate: The Canadian economics MA is almost universally 12 MONTHS — Toronto, UBC, McGill, Alberta, York. Calgary's thesis MA is CLOSED to applications. All fail the gate.
subjectFit.career: Central bank, government, research, consulting. Very good if that is the goal.
subjectFit.note: STRONG in Europe, where economics masters are typically 2 years. Keep Europe as the economics route and Canada as the quantitative-finance route.

subjectFit.subject: MSc Financial Engineering
subjectFit.whatItIs: Stochastic calculus, derivatives pricing, fixed income and term-structure modelling, numerical methods, Monte Carlo, risk management. The mathematics of exactly what he does at his desk, formalised.
subjectFit.admissions: Strong quantitative requirement. The CFA charter is directly relevant — Level II covers derivatives, fixed income and quantitative methods at similar depth. The Python work is a live demonstration.
subjectFit.funding: Because it is a research-stream degree it often qualifies for research funding — NSERC, FRQNT, Mitacs, entrance awards, plus differential-tuition exemptions for thesis-stream internationals.
subjectFit.career: Quant research, risk, structuring, treasury, model validation, central bank. Closest match to current work and best paid.
subjectFit.note: PRIMARY TARGET. HEC Montréal MSc Financial Engineering is the single strongest subject fit found.

subjectFit.subject: MSc Mathematics / Statistics (Thesis)
subjectFit.whatItIs: Pure methodology — probability, stochastic processes, time series, statistical inference, computational methods — then applied in a finance thesis.
subjectFit.admissions: A strong maths background is expected. This is the one genuine risk: a BSS in Economics may not carry enough measure theory or analysis. Address it head-on using the CFA quantitative content, the Python modelling and the 310-security model.
subjectFit.funding: The strongest of all. These departments guarantee funding as a condition of admission, because thesis students are research labour. Waterloo Applied Mathematics states support 'at a level that will cover academic costs and living expenses'.
subjectFit.lengthGate: Waterloo Applied Math 24 months · Queen's 16–24 months · McMaster 20 months · uOttawa 24 months. All clear the gate.
subjectFit.career: Quant, risk, data science, research. Employers read 'MMath' as quantitative competence.
